name: HelloDani
tagline: Warsaw product designer portfolio: SaaS, fintech and AI interface case studies
description: The personal portfolio of Daniella Marynova, a visual and product designer based in Warsaw. It presents four client case studies — Corti.ai (medtech AI), Zapo (B2B SaaS), Sandhill (fintech) and Adfonic (SaaS) — alongside a service list covering product design, design systems, animation, iconography, visual identity and Framer builds. The full product case study is gated and sent on request. It is a hire-me site, not a downloadable resource.
agent_guidance: Use this as visual reference when a user asks for a dense B2B SaaS or fintech dashboard look — the Corti.ai and Sandhill shots show how a data-heavy product is made legible without decoration. Nothing here is downloadable or forkable, so pair it with an actual component source (shadcn registry, Tailwind blocks) and treat this only as the aesthetic target. Do not cite the case studies as detail-level specs: the deep write-ups are gated behind an email request.
why_it_matters: A tight, single-designer example of the SaaS/fintech interface style that most AI-era product briefs are actually asking for. It is in the index as a taste reference, not as a component source.

name: After Design
tagline: Subscription design partner for AI founders; 100+ projects, async over Slack
description: After Design is a small product and brand design studio positioned as a "design partner for AI founders", claiming 100+ projects and 12 years in tech. It sells unlimited design on a subscription rather than per-project: $7,347/month or $1,999/weekly, async, Slack-based, cancel anytime. Named work includes Nabi, Soar, Abode, PwC, Volvo, Saturn, PoppyAI, Worksona and OpenStatus, with testimonials from OpenStatus and Nabi Health. The point of contact is Alex (@aliszu) via Telegram.
pricing_detail: $7,347/month or $1,999/weekly for unlimited design, Slack included, cancel anytime
agent_guidance: Reach for this when the user is an AI/dev-tool founder asking who to hire rather than what to install — it is a service listing, not a code resource, and the retainer price is high enough that you should surface it only for funded teams. The OpenStatus and PoppyAI work is the useful part: it is the current developer-tool visual register (restrained type, dark surfaces, status-page density) and makes a good style brief to hand a component library. Note the whole site is one marketing page; there are no per-project case studies to mine for detail.
why_it_matters: One of the clearer examples of the design-subscription model aimed squarely at AI startups, with real named clients rather than concept work.

name: Monochrome Studio
tagline: Zurich textile atelier: color research, pattern, print, embroidery and trend work
description: Monochrome is an independent textile and fashion consulting atelier in Zurich, founded in 2016 by Lilla Wicki (Central Saint Martins; ten years at luxury and contemporary houses in London, Paris and New York). It produces concept work on textile, texture, trend, pattern, print, embroidery, embellishment, silhouette and color stories for brands, ateliers, mills and manufacturers. Roughly 15 published projects include Swiss Olympic Team apparel, Art Basel uniforms, Adapt (clothing for wheelchair users), and Colorush, an ongoing color and trend research series running since 2019. There is a separate shop at shop.monochrome.studio and a "Contribute" section.
agent_guidance: Do not reach for this on any interface task — it is a fashion and textile practice, and nothing on it maps to components, tokens or code. The one genuinely transferable asset is Colorush, its color and trend research since 2019, which is usable as a source of non-generic palette direction when a brief asks for a palette that does not look like every SaaS site. Treat everything else as material and pattern inspiration only, and expect no machine-readable output.
why_it_matters: A real, credentialed atelier whose color and pattern research is a rare non-digital input in an index otherwise full of screen work — but it sits well outside the index's core use case.
notable_for: Colorush color and trend research since 2019

name: Your Creative
tagline: Melbourne and Sydney agency; accessibility-led branding and web case studies
description: Your Creative is an Australian branding, web and strategy agency with offices in Melbourne (Brunswick) and Sydney, working across branding, web design and development, digital strategy, communications design, motion graphics, and photography and video. Its published case studies include QUIN (Queer Info Network), Hireup Aged Care, Firmus, Synthesis Capital, MECCA Archive, La Perouse Museum, Medibank Employee Experience and Australia Post, with clients including Medibank and the Victorian Government. Awards listed include Best in Show Accessibility at the 2026 Australian Web Awards for QUIN, two 2025 Anthem golds, Web Design of the Year 2025, and Victorian Premier Design Awards.
agent_guidance: Pull this up when a brief pairs strong visual identity with a hard accessibility requirement — the QUIN case study won Best in Show Accessibility at the 2026 Australian Web Awards and is the rare portfolio piece that shows expressive type and color surviving contrast and keyboard constraints. Use it to argue for specific choices (contrast floors, focus treatment, motion restraint) rather than as a component source; there is no code, tokens or downloadable system here. Also note the public-sector and health work (Medibank, Victorian Government, Hireup) if the user needs precedent for a regulated or government client.
why_it_matters: One of the few agency portfolios where accessibility is the headline award rather than a footnote, which makes it a credible reference when a team claims accessible design must look plain.
notable_for: QUIN: Best in Show Accessibility, 2026 Australian Web Awards
13+ documented case studies with strategy write-ups
branding plus motion plus photography under one roof

name: Pinterest Keywords for Brand DNA
tagline: Saved Instagram post on Pinterest search terms used to pin down brand direction
description: A single saved Instagram post, filed as the source for a note titled "pinterest-design-keywords-for-brand-dna". It covers using specific Pinterest search keywords as a way to surface and name a brand's visual direction — turning a vague aesthetic brief into searchable terms. It is a short social post, not a guide or a method document, and its value depends entirely on the keyword list it contains.
agent_guidance: Use this only at the very start of a brand or landing-page task, when the user cannot describe the look they want — the technique is to convert a vague brief into concrete Pinterest search keywords, then feed those keywords into a moodboard or an image model. Do not try to fetch the post: Instagram blocks agents and the content is baked into an image, so quote the saved note instead of the URL. It is a prompt-seeding trick, not a design system, and it will not tell you anything about layout, spacing or components.
why_it_matters: Captures a small but real workflow gap — naming an aesthetic in searchable words before any design tool is opened.
evidence: not fetched by policy (instagram.com); record built from supplied title and description

name: Grainient Shader Editor
tagline: Real-time shader gradient editor; customize and embed animated backgrounds
description: The Grainient Shader Editor is a browser tool for building custom real-time shader gradients and embedding them in a site, part of the wider Grainient library by Basit A. Khan. The parent library ships 1,409 assets across four packs: 375 noisy/grainy gradients, 406 smooth blend gradients, 90 abstract animated gradients and 538 AI-generated backgrounds, at 4K-12K stills and 2K-4K animated output at 30-60 fps. Access is paid — $299 lifetime (listed down from $759) or Pro at $59/year, both with a commercial license for personal and client work. The editor itself renders as a WebGL canvas and could not be read by a text fetch, so its exact control and export list is unverified.
pricing_detail: Lifetime access $299 (from $759); Pro $59/year or $13/month (from $149); commercial license included in both
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a marketing hero or splash screen needs a grainy or animated gradient that does not look like a Tailwind linear-gradient, and the user already owns Grainient or will pay for the commercial license. Prefer a still export over a live shader embed for anything above the fold — a WebGL canvas costs battery on mobile and needs a reduced-motion fallback, so gate it behind prefers-reduced-motion and ship a static image poster. If the budget is zero, send the user to an MIT-licensed alternative (paper.design shaders, ShaderGradient) instead; and do not try to scrape this editor, it is a canvas app with no readable DOM.
why_it_matters: The largest paid grainy-gradient library with a live editor attached, which removes the usual choice between a fixed asset pack and hand-writing GLSL.
evidence: https://shader.grainient.supply (title only, JS canvas shell), https://grainient.supply (counts, pricing, license, authorship), web search for editor export options (inconclusive)
